items.title: Why Is My Kubernetes Job Still Pending? Tracing Kueue Admission with Headlamp
items.blurb: You submit a Kubernetes Job and wait for its Pods to appear. A minute passes. Then another. The Job is still suspended, there are no application logs, and there may not even be a Pod to inspect.

items.title: Netflix Bridges AWS IAM and Internal Identity with Workload Attestation
items.blurb: Netflix has developed a workload attestation mechanism for Apache Spark jobs running on Amazon EMR.

items.title: Cilium 1.20 Expands Gateway API and Opens eBPF Datapath for Kubernetes
items.blurb: Cilium 1.20 has been released with broader Kubernetes Gateway API support, an extensible eBPF datapath and further work on sidecarless mutual TLS.

items.title: The Shift to cgroup v2 in Kubernetes: What You Need to Know
items.blurb: In Linux, cgroups (control groups) are a kernel feature used for managing system resources.

items.title: GitHub Actions Runner Controller 0.15.0 Targets Reliability at Scale
items.blurb: GitHub has released Actions Runner Controller (ARC) 0.15.0, introducing reliability, scalability, and observability improvements for organisations running self-hosted GitHub Actions runners on Kubernetes. By Craig Risi

items.title: Presentation: Beyond the Prototype: Scaling Framework Agnostic AI Agent Infrastructure with Ray
items.blurb: The speakers discuss transitioning AI agents from local FastAPI prototypes to resilient production systems on Kubernetes using Ray.

items.title: Scaling Kubernetes Workloads with Node Swap
items.blurb: Memory is often the first hard limit a Kubernetes cluster hits. Nodes run out of RAM long before they run out of CPU, and the new wave of agentic AI workloads makes this worse.

items.title: Spotlight on SIG Apps
items.blurb: As Kubernetes adoption has grown, the conversation has shifted beyond running containers to managing increasingly complex application lifecycles.
